title: Confidential Database Query Engine with Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Traditional database encryption-at-rest models protect files on disk but force database servers to decrypt data into plaintext memory during query execution, exposing sensitive financial and healthcare records to rogue database administrators, memory-scraping malware, and cloud hypervisor compromises. Homomorphic Encryption (HE) solves this by enabling mathematical operations directly on ciphertexts without decryption. This project builds a confidential database query prototype in Python, TenSEAL, PostgreSQL, and Cryptography. The system encrypts sensitive numerical records client-side using BFV and CKKS homomorphic schemes, stores encrypted vector blobs in PostgreSQL, executes homomorphic SUM and AVG aggregations entirely on the server without plaintext access, and monitors ciphertext noise budgets to guarantee mathematical correctness upon client decryption.
use_cases: Healthcare research platforms aggregating encrypted patient clinical metrics across hospitals without HIPAA disclosures
Financial banking compliance audits verifying aggregate capital reserves without viewing individual customer balances
Confidential cloud database services offering zero-knowledge query processing on untrusted cloud infrastructure
hard_parts: Selecting and parameterizing BFV and CKKS homomorphic encryption polynomial modulus degrees and coefficient sizes
Tracking and managing ciphertext noise budget consumption across successive multiplication and addition operations
Executing homomorphic arithmetic operations across PostgreSQL bytea ciphertext vectors without memory exhaustion
Guaranteeing zero plaintext information leakage in database query logs, execution buffers, and temporary storage
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating client cryptographic key managers, homomorphic arithmetic engines, and PostgreSQL storage handlers
Zero-knowledge audit verifying that database query logs and server memory contain zero plaintext numerical records
Anti-fake verification script inserting dynamic encrypted payroll records and verifying exact decrypted mathematical sum parity

components.name: Homomorphic Cryptosystem Context & Key Manager
components.purpose: Generates BFV/CKKS public evaluation keys, secret keys, and Galois rotation keys with configurable parameters

components.name: Client Encryption & Decryption Module
components.purpose: Encrypts client plaintext vectors before transmission and decrypts aggregated server response ciphertexts

components.name: PostgreSQL Ciphertext Storage Layer
components.purpose: Stores serialized homomorphic ciphertext bytea arrays and associated non-sensitive relational attributes

components.name: Confidential Homomorphic Evaluation Engine
components.purpose: Executes homomorphic vector additions, multiplications, and scalar scalings directly on server ciphertexts

architecture.data_flow: The client Key Manager initializes BFV/CKKS cryptographic context parameters; public evaluation keys serialize and transmit to the server while private secret keys remain on the client; the client encrypts numerical records (e.g. salaries) and uploads ciphertext bytes to PostgreSQL; when an analytical query (e.g. SUM or AVG) arrives, the Confidential Evaluation Engine loads ciphertext byte arrays into memory; the engine performs homomorphic additions directly on ciphertexts without decryption; the resulting aggregated ciphertext byte buffer returns to the client; the client decrypts the payload using its private secret key, verifying noise budget and recovering the exact mathematical result.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic zero-knowledge guarantee: secret keys never leave the client; database server possesses only evaluation keys capable of arithmetic but incapable of decryption.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python programming, binary byte serialization, and SQL database operations
Understanding of applied cryptography concepts (public-key encryption, lattice cryptography, homomorphic properties)

environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source software stack via Docker Compose)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11 and PostgreSQL 15+ installed
environment.fallback_path: In-memory simulated Paillier or basic additively homomorphic cryptosystem if TenSEAL C-libraries encounter build issues

riskiest_component.name: Ciphertext Noise Budget Exhaustion Corrupting Decrypted Results
riskiest_component.fallback: Parameterize polynomial modulus degree to 8192 or 16384 to provide sufficient noise headroom for required arithmetic depth

deliverables: Git repository containing Python confidential query engine, TenSEAL wrappers, and PostgreSQL schema
Docker Compose file hosting PostgreSQL database with ciphertext tables
Automated confidentiality audit and mathematical precision verification test harness
Screener verification script executing automated benchmark and dynamic encrypted aggregation test in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) with arbitrary deep circuit bootstrapping
Custom lattice cryptography assembly optimizations for AVX-512 vector units
Hardware security module (HSM) PKCS#11 hardware token integration
safety_note: This project processes mock financial records and synthetic numerical vectors to demonstrate privacy-preserving database encryption. It does not handle real personal health information or live commercial banking assets.
resources: A Full (R)Homomorphic Encryption Scheme (Brakerski, Gentry, Vaikuntanathan BGV/BFV paper)
TenSEAL: A Library for Doing Homomorphic Encryption on Tensors (OpenMined)
Microsoft SEAL Architecture and Homomorphic Encryption Parameter Selection Manual

worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: HIPAA-compliant healthcare analytics, zero-knowledge financial audits, and confidential cloud databases.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: BFV/CKKS parameterization, noise budget management, ciphertext vector operations in PostgreSQL, and zero-leakage verification.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 5,000 numerical records with simulated account attributes and test queries. Synthetic records only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory Paillier simulation.
